page.layout: One printed page of running text, with a bare running head at the top and page number 28 at top left. Main text in one column full width. A heading "DIXI" centred mid-page. Below, a faint show-through of the reverse page (mirrored text) which is not transcribed.

main_text.l: sane inter famosas Thaidas castam Susannam aut Penelopen habere, quàm huius commatis Politicum, interquè Alcibiadem solito civiliorem, & Dionem solito inciviliorem, Cleomenem aliquem moribus civilem, gerentem se πολιτικῶς, Ciceronis verbo, hoc est, ut ego interpretor, nec Gnathonicè, nec Thrasonicè, verùm Thrasybulicè, jungendo exemplo Thrasybuli τῷ θεάσεα τὴν βουλὴν, ut absque adulationis fuco, sive Gnathonismo, ita absque jactantiæ vento, sive Thrasonismo.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page is present in the lower half and was omitted. The Greek words "τῷ θεάσεα" and "τὴν βουλὴν" are as printed in the scan; the first Greek word of the phrase "gerentem se" is printed as πολιτικῶς and may be imperfect. The heading reads DIXI in the scan, shown as a centred heading, possibly intended as the chapter number X with I; transcribed as printed.
